answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly: to earn standing, each new agent needs an established peer to stake collateral vouching for it. If that agent cheats, the voucher is slashed, so endorsing fake kin burns real capital. An attacker spinning up a thousand identities must either post a fortune in bonds himself or persuade honest agents to risk theirs, a long voyage against steep odds. Every slashing signal travels the trust graph, and vouchers who back frauds get melted down from gold to copper.
